records.title: 3.6L Direct-Injection Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
records.description: The 3.6L V6 (LFX naturally-aspirated and LF3 twin-turbo) uses direct fuel injection, so no fuel washes over the backs of the intake valves. Combined with a PCV system that routes oil vapor into the intake tract, carbon coking accumulates on the intake valves over time. By roughly 60,000-100,000 miles this can cause rough idle, misfires, hesitation, and reduced fuel economy/power. This is separate from timing-chain-stretch and high-pressure fuel-pump issues; it is a fueling/airflow deposit problem inherent to GDI engines.
records.solution: Clean the intake valves by walnut-shell media blasting (the accepted fix for GDI coking); chemical intake cleaners help mildly but do not remove hardened deposits. To slow recurrence, install an oil catch can on the PCV line and/or a reduced-orifice PCV to keep oil vapor out of the intake. Periodic top-end cleaning is preventive maintenance on these DI engines.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire codes

records.title: Brake Booster Pump Connector Corrosion (Recall 14062 — Fire Risk)
records.description: On 2013-2014 XTS vehicles built Feb 14, 2012 through Mar 7, 2014, a cavity plug on the brake booster (vacuum) pump connector can dislodge, allowing water intrusion and corrosion of the brake booster pump relay connector. The corrosion can create a resistive short that melts the connector, increasing the risk of an underhood fire and can compromise power-assist braking (hard/heavy brake pedal). This is GM safety recall 14062 (NHTSA campaign). Owners also report a related hard-brake-pedal complaint from poor connector seating on later cars.
records.solution: Have the recall (GM 14062) performed free at any Cadillac dealer: technicians apply sealant to the connector cavity plugs, re-route the vacuum pump vent hose, and replace the front body wiring harness as needed. If the connector or booster pump is already damaged outside warranty, replace the corroded connector/harness section and the vacuum/brake booster pump as required. Verify the recall is closed by VIN at the NHTSA or GM owner site.
symptoms: Melted or discolored connector at booster pump

records.title: Brake Lamps Flash Intermittently / Cruise Disengages (Recall — BCM)
records.description: Certain 2013 XTS (and 2013 ATS / 2014 Impala) vehicles have a body control module fault that causes the brake lamps to flash intermittently without the brake being applied, and can disengage the cruise control. The false brake-lamp flashing can mislead following drivers about whether the car is actually braking, raising crash risk — it became a federal safety recall (FMVSS 108) remedied by a BCM reprogram. Owners also report related quirks like hazard lights flashing on their own.
records.solution: Have the recall performed free at a Cadillac dealer — the remedy is a body control module software reprogram. If the symptom persists after the recall, inspect the brake-pedal position/stop-lamp switch and BCM connectors. Verify recall completion by VIN at NHTSA or GM owner center. Do not ignore, as it affects brake-lamp signaling and cruise function.

records.title: Electronic Parking Brake Actuator Failure
records.description: The electronic parking brake actuator motors on the rear calipers fail, either failing to apply or release the parking brake. A failed actuator can leave the parking brake stuck on one side, causing brake drag, heat, and uneven wear. The actuators are integrated into the rear brake calipers.
records.solution: Replace the rear brake caliper with integrated parking brake actuator on the affected side. Both sides should be replaced if the vehicle has high mileage. The new actuator must be initialized with a scan tool. Some aftermarket calipers include the actuator motor. Brake fluid flush is recommended during the repair.

records.title: HID Xenon Headlight Ballast Failure & Housing Moisture
records.description: XTS HID/Xenon headlamps suffer ballast (HID control unit) failures and headlight-housing condensation that cause intermittent or total loss of a low beam. Owners report flickering, a headlamp that cuts out then comes back, or a dead side after a new bulb. Moisture entering the housing is a frequent root cause — water reaching the ballast causes rapid failure — and corrosion in the headlight wiring/ground (often shared with the upper LED DRL) can take out both the ballast and DRL together.
records.solution: Diagnose by swapping the D3S bulb side-to-side; if the fault follows the position, the ballast/igniter is bad, not the bulb. Replace the failed HID ballast/control module and reseal the housing; dry out and re-gasket any housing showing condensation. Inspect the ballast connector and chassis ground for corrosion and repair before installing new parts, or the new ballast will fail again. Use OEM-grade D3S bulbs and a matching ballast to avoid color/flicker issues.
symptoms: One low-beam HID out or flickering
Headlight cuts out then comes back
Upper DRL out on the same side
New bulb still doesn't fix it

records.title: High-Pressure Direct-Injection Fuel Pump Failure
records.description: The engine-mounted high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) on the GM 3.6L direct-injection V6 is a known wear item that fails on the XTS, causing long crank/no-start (especially warm restart), rough idle, stalling and misfires. The most common codes are P0087 (fuel rail pressure too low), P0089 (fuel pressure regulator performance) and P0191 (rail pressure sensor), often with random misfire P0300. Because the high-pressure pump is cam-driven off the engine, a failing pump can drive adaptive fuel trims that mask early symptoms until it strands the car.
records.solution: Perform a live high-side fuel-pressure test during acceleration and on a warm restart to confirm the HPFP versus injectors or the low-pressure (in-tank) pump. Replace the high-pressure fuel pump and its sealing/lifter components; many shops also replace the camshaft pump-drive lifter and inspect the lobe. Use fresh GM-spec fuel-system sealant and torque to spec to avoid leaks. OEM HPFP PN 12641740 (supersedes 12622475; aftermarket Delphi HM10007 / GDP106 cross-references). Reset fuel trims after the repair.
symptoms: Extended crank or no-start, worse when warm

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Clicking / Blower Resistor No Heat
records.description: Two related HVAC complaints are common on the XTS: a repetitive clicking/knocking from behind the dash caused by a failing blend-door (temperature) actuator that can't reach its calibration stop, and loss of fan-speed control or no heat from a failed blower motor resistor/module — when the resistor fails the fan often works only on the highest setting. Owners report inconsistent temperature (one side hot/one cold) with the actuator fault and a dead or single-speed blower with the resistor fault.
records.solution: For the clicking: identify the failing blend-door actuator (listen/feel behind the dash while cycling temperature), replace the actuator and re-run the HVAC calibration/relearn. For no/limited fan: test the blower motor resistor/control module and the blower motor itself; replace the failed resistor module (and motor if it's drawing high current). Clear any HVAC actuator codes after replacement.

Blower only works on high speed
No fan / no air from vents
No heat or no cold air

records.title: Illuminated Door Handle LED Failure (Moisture)
records.description: The exterior approach-lighting LEDs in the chrome door handles burn out, leaving one or more handles dark when the car is unlocked. The dominant cause is water intrusion into the handle insert that corrodes/burns out the LED; early-production part numbers lack the rubber seal/grommet over the LED that later revised parts added. Less commonly the BCM or in-door wiring/connector corrosion is at fault. It's cosmetic but very frequently searched by XTS owners and trivially DIY-fixable.
records.solution: The handle insert (LED + lock-touch button) is sold as an assembly: pull the handle out, remove the rear screw, unplug and swap the insert. Use the latest revised part number that includes the sealing grommet to prevent repeat moisture failure. If multiple handles are dark at once, check the BCM exterior-lighting setting and the in-door wiring/connectors for corrosion before replacing LEDs.
symptoms: One or more door handle lights don't illuminate on unlock
Light worked then died after rain/car wash

records.title: Magnetic Ride Control (MagneRide) Strut/Shock Failure
records.description: XTS models equipped with Magnetic Ride Control use magneto-rheological dampers filled with a magnetically-responsive fluid. These MRC struts/shocks commonly leak, seize, or lose damping ability, often starting around 50,000-80,000 miles. Unlike a conventional strut that gets softer as it wears, a failing magnetic damper frequently locks up stiff or loses electronic control, and the sensors/wiring can trigger a 'Service Suspension System' message. OEM replacements are expensive because each damper is a mechatronic unit. Note: MRC was optional (standard front setup was HiPer Strut), so this affects only equipped cars.
records.solution: Replace the failed MagneRide damper(s); Cadillac recommends replacing in axle pairs. Owners commonly use OEM (AC Delco) dampers or lower-cost Arnott MagneRide-compatible units to retain the electronic suspension. A cheaper non-OEM path is a passive strut conversion kit that eliminates MagneRide (requires a resistor/block-off module to suppress the fault light). Verify wiring/connector integrity before condemning a damper.
symptoms: Harsh or crashy ride over bumps
Service Suspension System / Service Ride Control message
Visible fluid leak on strut/shock body

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Modules Not Entering Sleep Mode
records.description: XTS owners frequently report the 12V battery going dead overnight or after a few days of sitting, caused by a control module failing to enter sleep mode and continuing to draw current with the ignition off. Common culprits on this platform include the radio/CUE (infotainment) module and the BCM. Repeated deep discharges then prematurely kill the battery and can trigger low-state-of-charge warnings and start-stop faults. GM issued service information for low-battery-state-of-charge conditions on 2018-2019 XTS/ATS/CTS.
records.solution: Perform a parasitic-draw test (normal is under ~50mA once modules sleep, roughly 30-40 seconds after lockup) and pull-fuse isolation to find the circuit that stays awake. Common fixes include replacing/reflashing a faulty CUE/radio module or BCM, repairing a chattering switch/connector that wakes the bus, and removing non-OEM accessories (aftermarket LEDs are a documented trigger). Replace the battery if it has been repeatedly deep-cycled.
symptoms: Battery dead after sitting overnight or a few days
Low battery / reduced electrical features warnings

records.title: Passenger Presence System Fault / Passenger Airbag Light On
records.description: The front passenger seat contains a Passenger Presence System (occupant-classification sensor/module and wiring harness) that tells the airbag controller whether to enable the passenger airbag. On the XTS the sensor mat, the under-seat connector, and the wiring harness are prone to faults, illuminating the SRS/'Service Air Bag' warning and often leaving the PASSENGER AIRBAG OFF indicator stuck on (or incorrectly on with an adult seated). Because a fault can disable passenger airbag deployment, this is a genuine safety concern.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool for airbag/occupant-classification codes. First inspect, reseat, and clean the under-seat connector and wiring harness (corroded/loose pins are the most common cause). If the sensor/pressure-mat or Passenger Presence Module itself has failed, replace it; in some cases the sensor is integrated into the seat cushion, raising cost. A post-repair occupant-classification recalibration may be required.
symptoms: Service Air Bag / SRS warning light
Passenger airbag indicator stuck OFF with adult seated
Airbag light on after seat work

records.title: Rear Air Suspension Sudden Collapse (F38 Air Ride)
records.description: XTS models equipped with the optional rear air-leveling suspension (RPO F38) suffer sudden, total collapse of the rear air springs/struts, often without warning and sometimes at highway speed. NHTSA/CarComplaints reports describe the rear dropping so low the tires nearly contact the wheel wells, causing the rear end to bounce and loss of vehicle control. Root causes include failed rear air springs (perforation/dry-rot), a worn-out air dryer/desiccant that lets moisture accumulate, and air compressor/air-line failures. A 'Service Leveling System' message and the car sitting low or unlevel are the early warning signs. The 2013 model year alone shows ~24 logged suspension complaints, the highest-volume XTS problem after CUE.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool for leveling-system codes and a smoke/soap test of the air springs and lines. Replace failed rear air springs/struts and the air supply unit (compressor with integrated dryer). Many owners with repeat failures convert to a passive coil-spring/strut conversion kit (Strutmasters/Arnott) to permanently eliminate the air system. Always replace the air dryer/desiccant when servicing the compressor or moisture will quickly kill the new unit. OEM compressor assembly PN 84355910 (ACDelco 22956965); Arnott aftermarket compressor and spring kits are common cross-references.
symptoms: Rear end suddenly drops/sags, tires near wheel wells
Car sits low or unlevel at rest
Air compressor runs constantly or not at all
Rear bouncing / loss of control over bumps

records.title: Safety Alert Seat Haptic Motor Failure
records.description: The Safety Alert Seat uses haptic (vibration) motors in the left and right seat bolsters to pulse warnings for lane departure, blind spot, and forward collision. One side commonly stops vibrating (left or right only), or the system randomly switches between vibrate and chime. The documented weak point is a wire breaking where it enters the haptic motor assembly. Because GM ties this hardware into the driver-assist suite, a failed seat motor frequently also triggers a 'Service Driver Assist System' message.
records.solution: Confirm the dead side by triggering lane-departure to each side; if only one bolster pulses, the opposite motor/wire has failed. Replace the affected seat haptic vibration motor (left or right bumper-alert motor) and repair the broken wire at the motor entry. If the seat hardware checks out, scan the BCM for driver-assist codes and update software, since a glitch can mimic the failure. As a stopgap, owners can switch Alert Type to 'beeps' in the menu to restore audible warnings.
symptoms: No vibration on one side of seat
Seat randomly switches to chime instead of buzz
Lane-departure/blind-spot light flashes but no buzz

records.title: Service Power Steering Message (FWD Belt-Drive EPS)
records.description: Front-wheel-drive XTS models use a belt-drive electric power steering (EPS) system (AWD models use hydraulic). Owners report a 'Service Power Steering' message in the driver information center, usually after a cold start, sometimes with momentarily heavy/reduced steering assist. GM documents the condition with power-steering control module codes C056D 3C and C0475 00 and a BCM U0131, frequently traced to a poor G111 ground, a loose 80A F72UA fuse, or low battery voltage rather than a failed steering gear.
records.solution: Per the GM bulletin: inspect and clean the G111 ground (must be paint-free and tight), tighten the 80A F72UA fuse connection to 42 in-lb, fully charge/test the battery, then reprogram the power steering control module via SPS. Replace the steering gear/EPS motor only if codes persist after the ground/fuse/battery and reprogram steps. A weak battery or corroded connections is the most common true cause of the message.

records.title: Sunroof Drain Leak / Headliner Water Damage
records.description: The XTS dual-panel sunroof is prone to water intrusion that stains the cloth headliner and wets the front/rear passenger footwells. The design uses the same perimeter seal on the fixed glass as the moving panel (doubling leak-off) with undersized drain tubes that clog easily with debris, overwhelming the system in heavy rain. The problem became significant enough that Cadillac faced a class-action lawsuit over leaking sunroofs across several models. Water can also reach electrical modules under the carpet, causing secondary electrical faults.
records.solution: Flush all four sunroof drain tubes with low-pressure compressed air or a flexible trimmer line (avoid stiff wire that can pop the hose off at the bottom). Verify water exits at the rocker/A-pillar and rear quarter outlets. Replace cracked/age-hardened sunroof perimeter gaskets and reseat the drain hose grommets; in stubborn cases seal the leaking drain-tube connection. Dry and replace stained headliner/insulation and check for wet carpet over body control modules.
symptoms: Water dripping onto headliner or A-pillar
Wet front or rear floor carpet

records.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Stretch - XTS
records.description: The 2013-2019 XTS uses the GM 3.6L V6 (LFX, then LGX from 2016+) with the same timing chain stretch issue affecting CTS, SRX, and other GM 3.6L vehicles. The three timing chains and plastic guides wear prematurely between 80,000-120,000 miles. XTS models with the twin-turbo 3.6L (V-Sport) can have even earlier chain wear from the additional thermal stress.
records.solution: Complete timing chain replacement - all three chains, guides, tensioners, sprockets. Replace water pump simultaneously. Cloyes 9-0753S kit recommended. 10-14 hours labor.
symptoms: Check engine light with P0008, P0009, P0016-P0019

records.title: Torque Converter / Transmission Shudder (6T70/6T75)
records.description: XTS models with the 6T70/6T75 6-speed automatic exhibit a torque-converter-clutch (TCC) shudder felt as a vibration/'driving over rumble strips' sensation under light acceleration, typically 1000-1800 RPM in 4th/5th/6th gear, and a launch shudder from a stop. GM acknowledged the launch/upshift-downshift shudder in service bulletins covering XTS through 2019 with 6T70/6T75/6T80 transmissions; degraded transmission fluid that no longer holds the TCC friction material is the leading cause. A separate TSB (13120A) addresses a TCC solenoid sticking on debris.
records.solution: Per GM bulletins, the fix is a transmission fluid exchange/flush to the latest low-viscosity spec (the updated GM fluid restores TCC friction characteristics) and a TCM recalibration; severe cases need torque-converter replacement. Always verify the shudder isn't faulty spark plugs/coils (a common look-alike). Replace fluid with GM-approved spec only; inspect for a cracked flex plate if a vibration is present, since 6T70 converter-pilot cracks often crack the flex plate.
symptoms: Shake at steady highway cruise 1000-1800 RPM

records.title: Water Pump Weep-Hole Coolant Leak (3.6L V6)
records.description: The 3.6L V6 water pump develops an internal seal failure that lets coolant seep from the pump's weep hole — a designed indicator that the pump's internal shaft seal has failed. Owners commonly mistake the weep-hole drip for a 'pinhole' and try stop-leak, but it signals the pump is failing internally and will progress to overheating and potential head-gasket/engine damage. Low-coolant warnings, sweet smell, and white residue at the front of the engine are typical. RepairPal lists coolant leaks (pump, hoses, radiator) among the most common XTS cooling complaints.
records.solution: Confirm the source: clean the area and look for fresh coolant tracking from the weep hole below the water pump pulley (versus hose clamps or the radiator). Replace the water pump with a new OEM/ACDelco unit and gasket, refill with DEX-COOL, and pressure-test. Do NOT use stop-leak — it can clog the heater core and radiator. ACDelco Gold water pump PN 19325605 (aftermarket ACDelco 252-962 cross-reference); inspect the thermostat and upper/lower hoses while the system is open.
symptoms: Coolant dripping from weep hole / front of engine
White or orange crust on water pump
